{"self_assessment": "**Impact**
Our table built a fish with a clear outline: a rounded body, a forked tail fin, and a single run from the nose that splits top and bottom. By the last inspection about 153 of 157 dominoes would fall. The few that wouldn't are a small stub inside the fin's back edge, and the outline is complete without it. I took the bottom body line from the split to the tail. I also helped finish the tail joint and the fin edges. I can't say yet how the judge will read the result, but I think the shape holds up.

**Execution**
I traced the bottom line from the pad and checked the tail joint once it landed. I nudged a loose joint and closed a couple of small kinks near the fin. After a bump knocked down some dominoes on the fin's right edge, I stood them back up. I also ran an inspection that found the only unconnected dominoes, the stub on the back edge. In hindsight I could have flagged the stub earlier, and Jack's decision to leave it alone looks right to me.

**Collaboration**
I kept the table updated on what I was doing and which spots I was working on. I called out where Hana's and Jack's pieces looked off, and I tried to stay out of their corners so we didn't bump each other. I accept that one bump on the right edge still happened. I fixed it quickly and told Jack where I was working. Overall the team shared the work well. Sofia drew the pad, Jack and Hana did the tail halves, and I did the bottom body.

**Leadership**
I wasn't the one steering. Sofia set the plan and I backed it. I tried to keep energy up with light comments and clear status calls. I also supported the hands-off call near the end so we didn't risk breaking something that worked. If I did it again, I would take on more of the final checking and push to close the stub earlier."}
